---
title: Pull request
description: Reusable pull request template for scope, references, validation, and review readiness.
---

## 📖 Description

<!--
Describe what changes, why the change is needed, and any limitations.
Include compatibility, security, migration, or rollout implications where relevant.

Follow this repository's contribution and review process. If design or API
approval is required, link the agreed design and record its approval status.
Do not assume particular approval labels, languages, platforms, or build tools.
Explain why a separate spec is not needed when that decision needs clarification.
-->

## 🔗 References

<!--
Link related issues, tickets, pull requests, designs, or documentation.
If there is no tracking item, explain the context here.

For intermediate changes, use non-closing references supported by the tracker.
Close a tracking item only when all agreed implementation, validation, and
documentation are complete. Record deferred work separately.
-->

## 🔍 Validation

<!--
List each exact command run and its result. Include relevant manual steps,
environments, expected outcomes, and observed outcomes.
State what was not run and why. Do not present planned tests as passed tests.
For documentation-only changes, report documentation checks where available;
runtime tests may be not applicable.
-->

## ✅ Checklist

<!--
Mark completed items with [x]. For inapplicable items, add "Not applicable"
and a short reason rather than implying a check was performed.
Use this repository's actual required checks and contribution agreements.
-->

- [ ] Met applicable contribution requirements, including any required agreement.
- [ ] Linked a tracking item or explained the context.
- [ ] Recorded agreed scope and ownership where required.
- [ ] Linked required design/API approval or explained why no spec is needed.
- [ ] Kept the tracking item open unless this change completes the agreed work.
- [ ] Updated affected documentation, examples, and migration guidance.
- [ ] Updated contributor or automation guidance if workflows or conventions changed.
- [ ] Added or updated behavior tests where applicable and wired them into automation.
- [ ] Recorded actual validation results and any unverified scenarios.
- [ ] Passed applicable dependency, license, generated-artifact, and repository checks.

## 📋 Issue Type

<!-- Select the categories that apply. -->

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Task or maintenance
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Build, dependency, or automation change

<!--
Review the repository's actual CI results before marking the change ready.
Do not assume a particular CI provider, pipeline name, default branch, or
manual trigger. Explain failed or unavailable required checks and any remaining
review or rollout work.
-->
